evals.prompt: A stakeholder said: "I want a dashboard with a red banner that shows when inventory is low and also lets me export it to Excel." Turn this into proper requirement(s).
evals.expected_output: Splits into at least two atomic requirements (low-inventory alerting vs. export capability), rewrites the description away from the named mechanisms (red banner, Excel) toward the underlying capability, and gives each a rationale.

evals.prompt: Classify this: "The system shall encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.3 because we chose a cloud-hosted architecture." Is this a functional requirement?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a technological requirement (exists because of a chosen implementation, not an inherent business need), notes it should be tagged separately and held out of the business-requirements pass, and distinguishes it from a business-driven security requirement.

evals.prompt: Here are two requirements with identical wording: "The system shall display the user's order history." One came from a customer, one came from legal/compliance. Should they have the same priority?
evals.expected_output: Explains that rationale, not description, should drive priority; since the two have different rationales (convenience vs. compliance), they likely warrant different priority even with identical descriptions, and recommends writing out both rationales explicitly.
